scope: Scoped agent review of five complete final EXE mountain/river viewports at the calibrated 128-unit material period. All twenty material cards and eight other map views have their separate ground_identity_native_review.json.
observations: The inspected Yanshan mountain and tributary viewports retain continuous ground shading, narrow subdued blue-green headwaters and visible source-supported bends. Their thin angular cartographic lines remain apparent.
Hankou and Nanjing show connected main-channel ribbons with banks under the normal full HUD. The inspected desktop X30-layout Hankou frame preserves those water ribbons and material detail.
The new broadleaf fragments and pale jointed mineral ground are visibly different in the mountain views. Smaller motif scale reduces the oversized-leaf problem of the rejected integration candidate.

The frames still show hexagonal material/control edges, repeated leaf motifs across uniform ground, miniature-like mountain placement and dense unit/city overlap near Nanjing. These five views do not establish historical channel widths or commercial art parity.
remaining_visual_issues: Headwater bends and main-channel geometry remain angular at tactical zoom; river-bank widths are visual symbols, not measured historical widths.
Material/control boundaries still reveal polygons, and broad uniform regions still repeat their source motifs.
Mountain placement, near-view unit/city crowding, some label attachment and physical Motorola X30 acceptance remain outstanding.
